items.title: Will Gen Z vote out the BJP in ‘27? Sreenivasan Jain asks UP’s youth
items.summary: For nearly three months, young people have been protesting in Delhi and other cities. Will these protests have an electoral impact? Sreenivasan Jain travels to Uttar Pradesh, which goes to the polls early next year, to find out what the state’s Gen Z is thinking. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP won almost 30 fewer seats in the state than it did in 2019. In Sultanpur, Jain meets students at a coaching centre who are preparing for government jobs. Garima Verma, 23, has been preparing for the civil services for three years. She is critical of the state’s education system. “Compare primary schools in Bombay and Delhi with our primary schools here. That’s how big the difference is at our basic level,” she says.She wants the government to work on education and employment, but says it isn't responding. “Gen Z asks questions and nobody answers them.” Muskan Sahu, 21, is a first-time voter. “Look at any exam: UP Police, Lekhpal, NTPC, CGL, whatever you like. Paper leaks are a very big issue,” she says. She links these issues to the student protests in Delhi and criticises the crackdown. “Are we terrorists, that it gets them lathi-charged there?” In Mohanlalganj, Pratibhas Gautam, 21, tells us his mother earns Rs 10,000 a month doing sweeping and mopping work. On that income, the family cannot afford coaching fees for government job exams. Veer Bahadur, 24, voted for the BJP in 2024. He says there are no private sector jobs in rural areas like Mohanlalganj. He supports the protests in Delhi and other cities, and criticises the illegal detentions of protesters. A change in government, he says, is “absolutely necessary”. Not everyone agrees. Ram Anuj Dhuriya, 37, is preparing for the UPPCS exam. He has always voted for the BJP and says he will do so again. Nagendra Pratap, a local BJP worker, says the Delhi protests and the SIR have had no impact here. But he adds: “It’ll be a very tough election.” Complaining about the media is easy. As per the revised internship policy , only students who are in the last two years of their law courses would be allowed to undertake internships at the High Court. This restriction raised concerns over whether students who had completed their courses and were awaiting examination results or enrolment as advocates could continue interning with individual practising lawyers and attend court proceedings. " After hearing both sides, I think an interim order can be passed as far as the petitioner alone is concerned. The larger issue can be decided later, " the Court added. The office of the Charity Commissioner in Worli has been receiving complaints and caveats in a volume that would be unusual even for a busy civil court. These come from the Tata Trusts, from their chairman and his son, and from dissenting trustees. Every party is racing to be heard first, or at least not to be heard last. This article traces how a forum designed to protect charitable property has ended up determining whether the holding company of that group can hold a valid annual general meeting. It then asks whether the law, as it stands, is equipped for that role. How we got here The immediate trigger was legislative. By an Ordinance promulgated on September 1, 2025 , since replaced by the Maharashtra Public Trusts (Second Amendment) Act, 2025 , the State inserted Section 30A into the 1950 Act. The provision divides trustees into tenure and perpetual trustees. Unless the trust instrument provides otherwise , perpetual trustees may not exceed one-fourth of the total number of trustees. Where the instrument is silent on tenure, trustees may be appointed for up to five years at a time. Commentators were quick to notice the timing: after Ratan Tata’s death, the Tata Trusts had on October 17, 2024 passed a resolution on lifetime trusteeship , which became a point of contention in later disputes. The Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) is the second-largest shareholder in Tata Sons, behind the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT). A complaint alleged that three of SRTT’s six trustees are perpetual trustees, which would exceed the statutory ceiling; the Trusts reply that the amendment is prospective and does not touch earlier appointments . On May 15, 2026, the Charity Commissioner directed the Trusts to defer the board meeting fixed for May 16. The Trusts publicly described the direction as issued without notice or hearing. The direction was tied to that complaint, to a representation by trustee Venu Srinivasan and to the Bombay High Court’s order of May 13 allowing a petitioner to withdraw his writ petition challenging SRTT’s structure. SRTT has since remained unable to meet. The Commissioner ordered an inspector’s inquiry under Section 37 of the Act - with the Section 39 report still awaited - and consolidated the SRTT matter

items.title: High Court can order restoration of electricity in disputes involving power theft: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday held that High Courts can order the restoration of electricity supply that was disconnected over disputed allegations of theft, but advised against adopting a liberal approach in such cases [ Dakshin Gujarat Vij Vs Vaibhav Crusher ]. A Bench of Justices Manoj Misra and KV Viswanathan observed that electricity is essential for life and livelihood, and that its deprivation could have serious consequences. Therefore, constitutional courts can intervene to protect consumers against arbitrary disruption of electricity supply by electricity distribution companies, it held. " Electricity is an essential commodity necessary for both life and livelihood. Its deprivation may have serious consequences. In an appropriate case, the High Court may be justified in exercising its constitutional powers to protect a person from an arbitrary action of the State and its instrumentalities including a distribution licensee, " the judgment stated. The Court, however, cautioned that a liberal approach may not be appropriate in cases involving allegations of electricity theft. It said that in such cases - involving allegations of theft that are yet to be finally decided - courts should impose appropriate conditions before ordering the reconnection of electricity. "In cases of theft, which necessarily involves a criminal intent (i.e. mens rea), adoption of a liberal approach may not be appropriate. Rather, each case should be addressed on its own facts and if the facts so warrant, the High Court might be justified in even declining the prayer for restoration of electricity supply till entire amount, provisionally assessed, is deposited. In short, a circumspect approach is required while dealing with petitions seeking restoration of supply of electricity disconnected on ground of theft," the October 26 ruling stated. Justice Manoj Misra and Justice KV Viswanathan The judgment was delivered in appeals filed by Dakshin Gujarat Vij Company Limited and Paschim Gujarat Vij Company Limited against orders passed by the Gujarat High Court. One of the disputes concerned Vaibhav Metal Crusher, which had received a supplementary electricity bill demanding approximately ₹93 lakh towards alleged electricity theft, besides ₹23.45 lakh as compounding charges. The Gujarat High Court had permitted the restoration of electricity supply upon payment of 50 percent of the demanded amount and allowed the consumer to challenge the assessment of the demand. items.title: Dual PAN card case: Allahabad High Court grants bail to Azam Khan, refuses stay on conviction
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Thursday granted bail to Samajwadi Party leader Mohd Azam Khan and his son Abdullah Azam in the dual PAN card case [Mohd Azam Khan vs State of UP and 3 others]. Justice Samit Gopal suspended their sentences while their revision petitions challenging their conviction are pending. The Court observed that Khan and his son had already served substantial portions of their fixed-term sentences. "Looking to the nature of occurrence, period of detention of the accused/revisionists, the fact that the case in hand is for a fixed term of sentence, the present case is a fit case where the accused/revisionists... be enlarged on bail," the Court said. Justice Samit Gopal The case stems from a 2019 complaint by BJP leader Akash Saxena alleging that Abdullah Azam Khan in a planned conspiracy with his father procured a second PAN card with a forged date of birth to bypass age criteria to fraudulently contest the 2017 Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls from Rampur's Suar constituency. In November 2025, a Rampur Special MP/MLA Magistrate court convicted the accused under various provisions of Indian Penal Code and awarded up to 7 years of imprisonment. On appeal in May 2026, the Sessions Court enhanced the punishment up to 10 years for Azam Khan and seven years for Abdullah Azam. Appearing for the convicts, Senior Advocates Abhishek Manu Singhvi and N I Jafri , assisted by Advocate Shashwat Anand, submitted that while Azam Khan had undergone over four years and one month in custody, Abdullah Azam had served over three years and six months. Opposing the plea, Additional Advocate General Anoop Trivedi and counsel for the informant argued that the convicts actively forged statutory documents to manipulate elections. Admitting the criminal revisions, the High Court expedited the matter and listed it for final hearing in the third week of January 2027. While the Court granted bail to Khan and his son, it refused to stay their conviction. The denial of relief means they remain disqualified from contesting elections in view of the provisions of the Representation of the People Act, 1951. items.title: Madras High Court compares appointment of Srirangam pontiff to election of Pope, sets deadline to fill position
items.summary: The Madras High Court recently drew parallels between the election of the Pope and the appointment of the Srirangam temple's pontiff while ordering that the post which has remained vacant since 2018 be filled within six months [Veera Raghavan Vs State of TN] A division bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and P Murugan observed that those responsible for selecting the pontiff should remain inside the Mutt until a successor is chosen. " Just as the Cardinals are locked inside the Sistine Chapel and the doors are opened only when the white smoke emanates from the chimney indicating the selection of the Pope, the Sthalattars should be locked inside the Mutt premises and allowed to come out only after resolving the issue," said the Court. Justice GR Swaminathan, Justice P Murugan The Court was hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) petition filed by S Veeraraghavan, a devotee belonging to the Sri Vaishnava Tenkalai sect, seeking the appointment of a successor to the Sriranganarayana Jeeyar. The bench noted that the Jeeyars' lineage dates to the 12th century. Sri Ramanujacharya had devised an elaborate system for administering the Srirangam Ranganathaswamy Temple, with the Jeeyar occupying an apex position. Apart from performing spiritual functions, the Jeeyar exercises administrative responsibilities and acts as a neutral arbiter to ensure compliance with the Agamas. The 50th Jeeyar, who assumed office in 1989, died in 2018 without nominating a successor. Under the Mutt's customs, the successor must be selected by the Sthalattars, either unanimously or by majority. However, the Court observed that the prolonged vacancy benefited the Sthalattars and Bhattars, among whom the Jeeyar's powers had been distributed. " Since there is no Jeeyar, there is no one to question them also. There is no incentive for them to choose the next Jeeyar. On the other hand, the status quo suits them. But it certainly infringes the rights of the devotees. " The Court held that the failure to appoint a successor violates the fundamental rights of the Mutt's disciples under Article 25 of the Constitution. It noted that the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) Department had invited applications in 2021 and received responses from qualified candidates but had taken no consequential steps. It expressed shock that the previous Jeeyar had purportedly been appointed through proceedings issued by a temple official under Section 55(1) of the Tamil Nadu HR&CE Act, 1959.

items.title: Supreme Court strikes down Karnataka law protecting tainted appointments, questions High Court ruling
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday struck down Karnataka Civil Services (Validation of Selection and Appointment of 2011 Batch Gazetted Probationers) Act, 2022, which validated around 191 appointments that had earlier been cancelled over allegations of corruption and nepotism [Srinavasa T v State of Karnataka and Others] A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran held that the 2022 law was unconstitutional, as the State legislature could not overturn the cancellation of these appointments after the decision had been upheld by constitutional courts. Having set aside the 2022 law, the Court ruled that the appointments made pursuant to the tainted recruitment "will also come to an end." “We have no doubt in our minds that the subject legislation is unconstitutional,” the Court ruled. The Court declined to order fresh recruitment to these posts under the old rules. Instead, it directed the Karnataka government to notify existing Group A and B vacancies under the current recruitment rules. However, in a partial relief, the Court ordered age relaxation for untainted candidates and those who had approached the Court and Karnataka Administrative Tribunal (KAT). Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice Vinod Chandran The Court passed the judgment on appeals filed by Srinivasa T and others against two Karnataka High Court orders. The Court expressed “a little bit of surprise and a lot more alarm” at the Karnataka High Court’s handling of petitions that had challenged the enactment. “We cannot but record, a little bit of surprise and a lot more alarm, insofar as the impugned judgments are concerned. The PIL was cursorily dealt with, and the later Writ Petition was also dealt with in a similar manner, throwing to winds every tenet of law; upholding an enactment clearly beyond the scope of the powers conferred on the law-making authority and bordering on the absurd,” the bench said. items.title: Kerala High Court upholds relief to Wipro over 'Brahmins' sambar powder trademark
items.summary: The Kerala High Court recently upheld the temporary injunction imposed on Greenmount Spices, restricting it from using the ‘Brahmins’ or ‘Brahmins Sambar Powder’ trademarks until a trademark infringement suit filed by Wipro Enterprises is decided. [ Greenmount Spices Private Limited v. Wipro Enterprises Private Limited ] Justice CS Dias opined that Wipro had established a prima facie case to support its claim of prior commercial use of the trademarks in question. " I am satisfied that the respondent has established a prima facie case, supported by materials indicating prior commercial use of the ‘Brahmins’ trade mark. The balance of convenience is also in favour of the respondent. If the impugned use is ultimately found to infringe the respondent’s [Wipro] rights, its continued use may erode the distinctiveness of the trade mark and cause injury not readily compensable in damages. These conclusions are tentative and shall not prejudice the final adjudication of the suit, " the Court said in its judgment. Justice CS Dias In 2024, Wipro instituted a suit before a district court to restrain Greenmount from manufacturing, advertising, selling or exporting food products, including sambar powder, and from using Wipro's trademarks, or any identical or deceptively similar marks, including ‘Brahmins’ or ‘Brahmins Sambar Powder’, on packaging, websites or as a trade name or domain name. Along with the suit, Wipro filed an application for a temporary injunction against Greenmount. The district court allowed Wipro's application and temporarily injuncted Greenmount from using ‘Brahmins’ or ‘Brahmins Sambar Powder’ trademarks. Greenmount subsequently moved the High Court challenging the district court's temporary injunction. They claimed that their trademark is ‘Greenmount’, whereas ‘Brahmin Sambar Powder’ is used only descriptively to identify the product, not as a trademark. They argued that the word ‘Brahmin’ denotes a traditional Hindu community and and sambar is an integral part of their cuisine. This makes the expression ‘Brahmin Sambar Powder’ a generic and descriptive one that is protected by Section 30(2)(a) of the Trade Marks Act, 1999. Wipro opposed Greenmount's appeal pointing out that it acquired the Brahmins group business together with its trade mark and goodwill and is now the owner of the trade mark ‘Brahmins’. items.title: Supreme Court reserves verdict on ED's Article 32 plea for CBI probe against Mamata Banerjee
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday reserved its verdict on a petition filed by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) seeking a probe by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) into alleged obstructions during its search operations at the Kolkata premises of political consultancy firm I-PAC [ ED v. State of West Bengal & Ors. ]. The matter concerns an incident from January 8, when TMC leader and the then West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, entered the premises of political consultancy firm Indian Pac Consulting Private Limited (I-PAC) and allegedly took away certain sensitive files. A Bench of Justices PK Mishra and NV Anjaria reserved orders after hearing arguments on behalf Banerjee, the ED, and other respondents. "Arguments concluded, reserved for order/judgment," the Court said. Justice PK Mishra and Justice NV Anjaria The ED had moved the top court under Article 32 of the Constitution, alleging that on January 8, Banerjee and senior State police officials barged into I-PAC's Kolkata office and the residence of its co-founder Pratik Jain while searches were underway in connection with a 2020 coal smuggling money laundering case against businessman Anup Majee. The agency claimed that the intervention resulted in the forced removal of critical physical and electronic evidence. Banerjee, however, maintained that the material pertained solely to her political party (Trinamool Congress), which has been associated with the consultancy firm since 2019. The ED had initially moved the Calcutta High Court against the alleged interference, but was compelled to approach the Supreme Court after proceedings in Kolkata could not take place due to an unruly commotion inside the courtroom. When the matter first came up before the apex court on January 15, the Bench had observed that failing to examine the issues would lead to "lawlessness," and issued notice to Banerjee, Director General of Police (DGP) Rajeev Kumar, and others. During subsequent hearings, the maintainability of the plea came under sharp scrutiny. The State - then led by the TMC - contended that Article 32 is a constitutional remedy meant solely for citizens to enforce fundamental rights against State excess, and cannot be invoked by an investigating agency. Justice Brijeshkumari Rameshwarsinh Rajput , presiding over the Third Additional Sessions Court in Gandhinagar's Kalol held that cows could become extinct if people who slaughter them are not punished in accordance with the law. items.title: Tiger Shroff firing case: Special MCOCA court remands 11 accused to police custody till November 6
items.summary: Eleven persons, including two women, accused in the case registered after gun shots were fired towards Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff in Juhu have been remanded to police custody till November 6 by a special court designated to hear cases under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act, 1999 (MCOCA). Special Judge Satyanarayan Ramjivan Navandar passed the remand order on October 29. The Mumbai Police Crime Branch sought 10 days of custodial interrogation to probe a wider syndicate conspiracy. The invocation of MCOCA was sanctioned by the court on October 28 after the prosecution cited the criminal antecedents of six of the accused. The prosecution also cited financial motives, and an alleged bid to establish gang dominance. The Crime Branch informed the court that wanted operative Anil Pandit, suspected to be affiliated with the Lawrence Bishnoi syndicate and facing three chargesheets in Punjab and Haryana, had claimed responsibility for the assault through social media and audio messages. Police further submitted that three shooters admitted during interrogation that the October 18 attack on Shroff was their third attempt on Pandit’s directives. According to the prosecution, the assailants opened fire, discharging five to six rounds at Shroff’s vehicle on the evening of October 18 as he was exiting a football ground in Juhu. While the actor escaped unhurt, his driver and a bystander sustained bullet injuries. The Mumbai Police subsequently registered an FIR for attempt to murder alongside offences punishable under the Arms Act. The investigation has pointed to transnational coordination linked to the Lawrence Bishnoi syndicate. Custodial interrogation of the accused is underway to trace the illicit financial trails and determine the broader motive behind the targeted shooting.

items.title: Supreme Court to vet RBI’s digital fraud regulations before notification, says banks must compensate victims
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday said that it would examine the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI’s) proposed anti-cyber fraud regulations before they are notified. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing suo motu proceedings concerning digital arrest scams. The case arose from a senior citizen couple’s complaint of losing ₹1.05 crore to impersonators using forged judicial orders. It said that the regulations must require financial institutions to compensate victims where fraud results from failed due diligence. Compensation must be at least equivalent to the customer’s loss, the Court said. “The amount will remain intact. The bank will have to pay. That is the only way,” the CJI remarked, stressing that liability could not stop with individual officers. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana Justice Bagchi questioned why financial institutions should not face strict liability when their failure to provide safeguards enables misuse of banking products. Banks must become a “protective umbrella” for customers, the CJI said, asking why an unusually large transfer from a pensioner’s savings should not trigger intervention. The Court emphasised mandatory suspension of unusual transactions, automated reporting and physical verification of genuineness. “ Do they have sufficient teeth to control it?” the CJI asked about RBI’s regulations. “Unless there is a penal direction to these banks, they will never mend their ways.” He questioned the RBI’s “soft-pedalling” through consultations with banks when action was sought against them and contrasted banks’ loan settlements with their accountability towards victims. Justice Bagchi sought data on suspicious transactions blocked and those unreported before fraud subsequently emerged. Appearing for the RBI, Attorney General for India R Venkataramani said that bank employees had also prevented fraud and complaints had fallen by about 50%. He sought time for technical integration, proposing notification by November 30 and operationalisation by December 31. The Bench sought the draft regulations and a list of authorised financial institutions. “The regulation must include a liability clause. Otherwise, we will enforce it through a judicial order,” the CJI said. Attorney General R Venkataramani Senior Advocate NS Nappinai , the amicus curiae assisting the Court, said that scams continued despite awareness campaigns and proposals for lagged payments

items.title: NLUO announces Double Credit Course on Economics of Competition Law

With over a decade of litigation experience, her practice spans across constitutional law, service law, arbitration, antitrust, and financial regulation. She has judged leading international moots, including the Jessup, Willem C. Vis East, and FDI International Arbitration Moots. items.title: Byju's insolvency: Drama in Kerala High Court after judge flags out-of-turn listing; bench split on stay order
items.summary: Drama unfolded in court room 6D of the Kerala High Court on Thursday after a judge, sitting as part of a division bench, took exception to the out-of-turn listing of a case despite an earlier order stating that the matter was to be heard only on November 6. Justice Johnson John , the junior judge on the bench, said that the earlier order had clearly spelt out that the case was to be listed only on November 6 and that he was unaware as to why it came up for hearing today. “ I don’t want to explain further...I don’t know why it came up today. It was posted for November 6,” Justice John said. The case pertained to the ongoing insolvency proceedings against Think and Learn Private Limited, which owns edu-tech firm Byju’s. Listed before the Court was a review petition filed by Voizzit Technology (a creditor who has claimed right to the ownership of Byju’s) challenging the dismissal of a writ petition filed by it earlier seeking a probe into the insolvency proceedings. A Bench of Justices K Natarajan and John had earlier issued notice on the the review petition filed by Voizzit during an October 27 hearing and posted the case for further consideration on November 6. However, the matter came to be listed today, with Justice John repeatedly expressing that this was done without his knowledge. The Bench, however, added that they were unable to agree on whether the judgment under review should be stayed while the review petition was pending. “ We are having divergent opinions, that's why we have not stayed the appeal ,” said Justice Natarajan. “ There is a difference of opinion regarding the question of stay. So, in such circumstances, the matter has to be placed before the Registry, which will place it before the Chief Justice ,” added Justice John. Justice K Natarajan and Justice Johnson John This prompted Vozzit’s counsel, advocate PC Sasidharan, to raise an objection. Sasidharan claimed that today’s split opinion and reference to the Chief Justice amounted to changing the order passed by the High Court in the last hearing of the matter. It was his argument that the judges were unanimous on October 27 as regards the stay order. “Separate order must be there, My Lord, independently, and we should be given copy and it should be uploaded, but it is not seen as uploaded. items.title: Kerala High Court halts arrest of MACT judge booked after his minor son causes fatal car crash
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Thursday granted interim protection from arrest to the Additional District Judge whose son was recently involved in a car crash that killed a scooter rider. Justice Kauser Edappagath passed the order on an anticipatory bail plea moved by the judge. "The police shall not arrest the applicant until further orders. However, he shall appear before the investigating officer today at 1:00 pm and if necessary as and when called for. The interrogation of the applicant shall be done in accordance with the guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court," the Court ordered. Justice Kauser Edappagath Senior Counsel P Vijaya Bhanu , appearing for the accused- judge, told the Court that he appeared before the police yesterday and was interrogated for over 4 hours. Another notice to appear before the police has since been issued, Bhanu added. The bench questioned the necessity of custodial interrogation and further said that since the accused is a judge himself, he will cooperate with the probe. "What was the need to interrogate him for 4 hours and now for further interrogation? Why is his arrest required? He is a judicial officer. He will co-operate with the investigation," the Court remarked. Kerala High Court Why is his arrest required? He is a judicial officer. He will co-operate with the investigation. The counsel representing the legal heirs of the victim of the crash opposed the plea. He submitted that the accused judge tampered with evidence once he was informed of the accident. However, the Court said that it has to go strictly as per law and granted protection from arrest to the accused. The Court also asked the prosecutor to furnish the State's response/ instructions on the plea. The accused-judge's 17-year-old son was driving a Mercedes-Benz car when he hit a two-wheeler in Kochi's Cheranalloor on October 25, killing the scooter rider, one Jayabalakrishnan. The judge who is posted at a Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) at Iranjalakuda in Thrissur district, was arraigned as an accused in the FIR registered by the Police after the crash. items.title: Kerala cops arrest BLM co-op society chairman in Chennai for alleged fund diversion
items.summary: The Kerala Crime Branch Police on Thursday, October 29, arrested R Premkumar, founder chairman of Bharath Lajhna Multi State Cooperative Society, one of the leading co-operative societies in Kerala and Tamil Nadu. Premkumar was taken into custody from his residence in Chennai. Crime Branch officials, however, refused to divulge details of the case. The case is being probed by the Economic Offences Wing of Crime Branch, Kozhikode. A team led by DySP, Crime Branch, EOW, arrested Premkumar. Following the arrest, Premkumar complained of physical discomfort and was shifted to a hospital. As per reports, funds worth Rs 300 crore were siphoned off to the private accounts of Premkumar. The money collected as deposits from members of the cooperative society was diverted for purchase of resorts and theatres, allegations said. The case began with the former CEO Naveen S Nair filing a complaint with the Nadakavu police station in Kozhikode against Premkumar and a few others for physically attacking him. He later withdrew the complaint, but the Crime Branch, having found some evidence of misappropriation of funds of the society, went ahead and registered an FIR invoking section 316 (5) (criminal breach of trust) and 318 (2) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita against the accused. According to reports, the Crime Branch has found misappropriation of funds worth crores from the society to the personal bank accounts of Premkumar and his close relatives. The Crime Branch is learnt to have identified around 320 bank accounts which allegedly belonged to Premkumar and his close relatives. BLM reportedly has around 150 branches and over 15 lakh members across Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry. It was started in Chennai in 2006 as a housing co-operative society with a focus on the development of housing activities.

items.title: The path of Cyclone Arnab went through India's plans for data centers and future growth
items.summary: By Sibi Arasu A cyclone that powered up over unusually warm ocean waters hit part of India's coastline that's dense with billions of dollars of investment in data centers , underscoring the threats to infrastructure as extreme weather becomes more frequent. Cyclone Arnab battered parts of eastern Andhra Pradesh state Wednesday, killing three people, damaging homes and infrastructure and inundating roughly 200,000 acres of cropland, according to state authorities. Heavy rainfall was the biggest threat inland as the storm weakened. Meteorologists said unusually high temperatures across the Bay of Bengal helped fuel Arnab. Its arrival on a coastline where billions of dollars are being invested in data centers at early stages of construction underscored how extreme weather threatens both existing livelihoods and the infrastructure intended to drive future growth, climate experts said. It will likely take days or weeks for full damage estimates to be calculated. Warmer seas and a faltering monsoon Unusually high temperatures across the Bay of Bengal, an already warm atmosphere and heat stored below the surface helped fuel Arnab, according to K.J. Ramesh, a former director general of the Indian Meteorological Department. “A warmer atmosphere can also hold more moisture, increasing the potential for intense rainfall,” he said. The unusually warm waters also helped the storm strengthen rapidly, according to Akshay Deoras, a weather expert at the University of Reading in the United Kingdom. He said cyclones are part of natural weather patterns but warming from human-caused climate change can amplify their rainfall. The storm follows India’s weakest southwest monsoon since 2015. A strong El Niño weather phenomenon combined with an already warming climate has resulted in sparse rainfall from June through September, according to weather experts. Districts across several Indian states have declared droughts and southern and eastern India suffered particularly large deficits. Intense downpours offer little reassurance when rain falls unevenly. Heavy rainfall can also run off hardened, dry ground, rather than being absorbed. The economic damage spreads beyond the coast Past extreme weather has already been devastating in India. items.title: MP Owaisi seeks transparent plan to tackle El Niño impact on Hyderabad’s water supply
items.summary: Hyderabad MP and All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) president Asaduddin Owaisi has called for a clear plan to address drinking water security in Hyderabad and surrounding urban areas, as well as a dedicated summer action plan that includes urban employment guarantee provisions to deal with the impact of El Niño on Telangana. In an October 28 letter to Deputy CM Bhatti Vikramarka, who is heading the Cabinet sub-committee charged with dealing with the drought and El Niño conditions across Telangana, Owaisi made several suggestions, including a dedicated urban summer action plan addressing the specific vulnerabilities of Hyderabad, Cyberabad, Malkajgiri and the surrounding urban regions. Amid concerns over drinking water security for Hyderabad and the Core Urban Region, Owaisi called on the government to publish a dedicated drinking water plan for the summer season for Hyderabad and surrounding urban areas, including source-wise availability, zone-wise supply schedules, and cut-off dates for contingency sourcing, through a public-facing dashboard. He noted that storage in the reservoirs supplying water to the Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWSSB) have all fallen below normal levels, with the Singur and Manjeera dams almost dried up. He also asked the HMWSSB, the irrigation department and the Mission Bhagiratha drinking water project to publish a monthly water account showing legally available shares, minimum drawdown levels, and monthly demand for the Core Urban Region. Referring to the depleted groundwater levels in the city, Owaisi suggested that commercial water suppliers must be required to disclose their source and the authorised daily withdrawal. He also requested that the government set aside small tankers for Old City neighbourhoods with narrow lanes, with a telephone and offline booking route. While the government has declared 365 mandals as drought-hit for the 2026 kharif season, Owaisi said that this is mainly a rural drought response framework and that Hyderabad too needs a dedicated urban summer action plan. The plan should include drinking water security, water kiosks, urban employment, ORS distribution, animal water, cooling centres, and special protection for women, children and the elderly, the letter said, stressing that a coordinated, time-bound and transparent response is essential.

items.title: Centre says tribal leaders are not ‘necessary’ parties to Great Nicobar forest rights dispute
items.summary: The Union Tribal Affairs Ministry has said that Nicobarese leaders seeking to join a petition challenging the settlement of forest rights on Great Nicobar Island are “neither necessary nor proper parties,” in the case, court documents show. The Nicobarese are one of two major tribes affected by the development of the Island, and primary claimants to forest rights in the area. An ongoing petition in the Calcutta High Court, filed by former IAS officer Meena Gupta, has challenged the Union government’s claim that rights under the Forest Rights Act (2005) (FRA) were settled on the Island. The FRA recognises the historical rights of tribal and other forest dwelling communities over forest resources, and makes compliance with its statutes necessary in clearing forest land for diversion. On July 9, 2026, four Nicobarese residents sought to join Gupta’s plea, arguing that government certifications claiming the settlement of forest rights was based on gram sabha consent from non-tribal settler communities. Apart from the Nicobarese and Shompen — a particularly vulnerable and largely uncontacted tribe — the Island is inhabited by families of ex-servicemen from the mainland who were settled on the remote Island from 1969 onwards as part of a state-sponsored scheme. “This certificate falsely states that the concerned Gram Sabhas have consented to the diversion of forest lands and cites meetings of the Gram Sabhas of the settler community in which no Nicobarese were present,” the impleadment document submitted to the court, seen by Mongabay-India, says. “No Gram Sabha meeting of the tribals was ever convened to discuss the issue of diversion of forest lands for the mega-project,” it adds. A long-standing demand of the Nicobarese has been to return to their ancestral villages after they were displaced by the 2004 tsunami. Parts of this land will be diverted for the Great Nicobar Island development project. A boat approaches Nicobar Island. items.title: Kochi private buses race, road users at risk
items.summary: Kochi has a frequent and active network of private city buses. However, commuters in the city also have to contend with the aggressive and reckless driving style of Kochi's private buses. Drivers hurry to reach their destinations at high speed, often without considering other vehicles on the road. Minor accidents and near-miss incidents have become very common on these roads. Commuters in Kochi city complain about unnecessary honking, sudden overtaking, and minor accidents involving private buses, especially during peak hours. According to a statement issued by the Kochi police, they registered 2,003 cases against bus crew members during inspections conducted between September 9 and 30. Among these, 130 cases were registered for competitive driving, and 71 involved dangerous or negligent driving. Speaking to TNM, KM Siraj, Private Bus Owners Association, Ernakulam District secretary, said there is no system on our roads to maintain a safe distance between buses, two-wheelers, and cars. "Such systems may exist on national highways, but there is no such arrangement in cities," he added. He also said, “If the workers are found guilty in the police’s current legal proceedings against them, we too will agree with and cooperate with those actions."

items.title: ‘Demonic portrayal’: Chennai Mayor Priya objects to Galatta Media reels
items.summary: Greater Chennai Corporation Mayor R Priya has issued a legal notice to Galatta Media Private Limited on Wednesday, October 28, objecting to social media reels that allegedly portrayed her as a demonic figure using visual effects and background music. The legal notice, issued through the firm Saravanan and Partners, alleges that Galatta Media – which runs a YouTube channel – published and circulated her videos on its official Instagram and YouTube Shorts accounts with horns superimposed on her image, red lighting and music intended to evoke the impression of an evil or demonic character. According to the notice, the video was taken at a public event where Priya was seated on a stage alongside other dignitaries. The mayor objected to four Instagram reels and one YouTube Short. The notice alleged that the same video was uploaded multiple times on Instagram, each time with different accompanying music, to maximise its reach and repeatedly damage her public image. “The objection arises from the combined effect of the altered visual representation, the horns graphically placed upon her image, the accompanying background music and the overall manner in which the content has been edited and presented to viewers,” the notice stated. The notice said that the combination of the visual effects, music and editing created an impression capable of inviting hatred, ridicule and contempt towards Priya. The notice also distinguished between criticism of a public representative and visual representations that degraded an individual's dignity and reputation. Priya, according to the notice, recognised the importance of freedom of speech and expression and the media's role in a democracy. However, it argued that her position as mayor did not give others an unrestricted licence to subject her to degrading visual portrayals or gratuitous personal ridicule. “The exercise of editorial freedom by a media organisation does not, by itself, answer the legitimate concerns arising from the manner in which an identifiable person's image has been used,” the notice stated. The legal notice comes amid a series of complaints by Priya over alleged online harassment and the circulation of edited or morphed images and videos of her.
